summary: Discovery call to understand Nova Payments' integration needs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment options. Primary focus: SDK compatibility (LangChain/LlamaIndex), running behind a gateway/proxy, rate limits and quotas, observability hooks and security (SAML, KMS, VPC). Agreed to share integration examples and run a latency benchmark with customer prompts.
topics: Rate limits, quotas, and headers for client throttling
Observability hooks: tracing, tokens/cost breakdown, per-route dashboards
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/KMS) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-14 | Time: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Zhou (Redwood SE), Arjun Mehta (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Nova Payments), Roberto Diaz (Nova Platform), Emily Cho (Nova Security), Kai Turner (Nova SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, I'll kick us off - I'm Samir from Redwood inference, AE on this account. Lina and Arjun from our SE team are here. how's everyone?
[00:12] Maya: hey, thanks - good, excited to talk through integration options. we are trying to understand how Redwood would fit into our payments stack - specifically SDKs, latency and private deployment options.
[00:25] Roberto: yeah hi - we run most inference through an internal gateway; we need to see how the SDKs integrate and whether a proxy in front would add too much latency.
[00:38] Lina: great context, thanks. quick agenda: 1) current stack and constraints, 2) SDKs/langchain patterns, 3) hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), 4) rate limits/quotas, 5) observability hooks, then next steps. ok?
[00:50] Maya: sounds good.
[00:55] Roberto: quick note - we care about p95 latency under 200ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) and throughput at peak of ~200 RPS.
[01:05] Arjun: noted. what model sizes are you considering? small-ish or larger?
[01:10] Maya: we plan to run an open Llama-variant for in-house personalization, but also want fallback to higher-quality hosted models for complex responses.
[01:22] Lina: perfect - that's a common pattern. for SDKs we provide python and node client libs, and we have example LangChain connectors and LlamaIndex adapters. we can share a notebook; it's pretty straightforward to swap our endpoint into existing LangChain chains.
[01:36] Maya: do you have examples for the gateway/proxy auth flow? we run a JWT-based internal gateway that sets x-forwarded-user headers and does mTLS to external services.
[01:48] Samir: yes, we commonly see two patterns: 1) gateway routes to Redwood hosted API using short-lived service tokens (recommended for hosted) and 2) for Dedicated/Private you run a local sidecar or an internal endpoint - basically mimic the same interface so you don't need to change LangChain calls. we have sample proxy config in our docs (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/integrations/gateway-proxy).
[02:10] Roberto: any extra latency for the hosted option when routing via our gateway? rough numbers?
[02:17] Arjun: the extra hop is usually tens of ms; main delta is network egress to Redwood region. for short prompts your biggest gains are in model selection and batching config. for Dedicated we can put the capacity in same cloud region to hit single-digit ms inter-node times.
[02:33] Maya: ok. on auth - we need SAML SSO for console and SSO for API keys rotated via our KMS. how does Redwood handle key management?
[02:44] Samir: for Hosted we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for private deployments? let me rephrase - Hosted supports Redwood-managed keys by default, but for Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and to sign tokens. also we support SSO/SAML for console access and RBAC.
[03:05] Emily: do you have SOC 2 and audit logs?
[03:08] Lina: yes SOC 2 Type II, we can share the security pack. we stream audit logs for Dedicated/Private; Hosted exposes detailed usage logs and per-token cost breakdown in the console. we'll share the security docs after the call.
[03:23] Maya: perfect. can you explain rate limits and quotas - we need bursts but fair scheduling; also, how do you surface client headers and tracing?
[03:33] Arjun: we expose rate-limit headers that are standard: x-rw-rate-limit, x-rw-rate-remaining, etc. You can set per-key quotas on Hosted and per-tenant quotas on Dedicated. For high throughput we recommend configuring token-batching and prefix caching to reduce token compute. For tracing, we support OpenTelemetry hooks and a tracing id header you can pass; it surfaces in the Redwood console.
[03:58] Kai: is there example code to wire OpenTelemetry from our gateway through to Redwood so traces join end-to-end?
[04:05] Lina: yes we have sample middleware for Node/Express and Python that forwards traceparent and baggage. I'll attach sample code. (note: some customers reported small mismatches in trace ids with older SDK versions - that's been fixed in v2.1.1)
[04:25] Maya: cool. about LangChain and LlamaIndex - can we reuse our existing chains or do we need to refactor?
[04:32] Arjun: typically just swap the client. LangChain has an LLM wrapper that points to the Redwood SDK endpoint; LlamaIndex uses the same transport for embeddings and index queries. we provide example connectors: LangChain -> RedwoodLLM, LlamaIndex -> RedwoodEmbeddings. we also include a sample caching layer to reduce repeated embeddings.
[04:55] Roberto: embeddings - do you host them or push to a vector DB? we use Pinecone for similarity search; what's typical?
[05:03] Lina: many customers use Redwood for generating embeddings then push to Pinecone/Weaviate. Redwood also offers vector storage integrations (we can export in batch). for latency-sensitive search we recommend local indexer with async embedding ingestion.
[05:20] Maya: question on quotas - when you talk about per-key quotas for Hosted, can we map quotas to internal teams via a single org key?
[05:29] Samir: yes, you can create sub-keys with quotas and tags; console shows per-route cost and token breakdown so teams can be billed internally. For Dedicated we can carve out capacity reservations per-team.
[05:44] Emily: for Private/VPC option - does Redwood provide an air-gapped on-prem bundle? and how is deployment managed?
[05:52] Lina: yes we have an on-prem package for regulated customers. it's delivered as a set of Helm charts and a control plane can be run in your VPC. We support KMS via HSM and do not exfiltrate logs without customer opt-in. setup requires our infra team for initial deploy and we do a runbook handoff.
[06:12] Maya: cost - high level, how different is Dedicated vs Hosted? we need ballpark numbers to present to procurement.
[06:19] Samir: Hosted is pay-as-you-go per-token/per-embedding - good for variable workloads. Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly/annual commit) so unit cost drops and you get isolation. I'll send a pricing example for your throughput numbers.
[06:34] Roberto: can we do a POC with a small dedicated slice or do you need full commit?
[06:39] Arjun: we offer short-term dedicated pilot pools for benchmarking; it's a smaller reservation and limited time. we'll outline options in the proposal.
[06:49] Maya: observability - specifically, we want per-route latency and per-token cost in our observability stack. do you expose APIs or hooks?
[06:58] Lina: console has per-route dashboards, but we also surface telemetry via API and event webhooks (usage, errors, alerts). you can ship traces to your tracing backend via OpenTelemetry and export logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[07:15] Kai: if we put a gateway in front, will logs still show the original end-user id or will Redwood just see gateway identity?
[07:24] Samir: you can forward original user headers; we support forwarded attributes but you need to sanitise PII. for audit logs we store actor as the API key unless you pass x-rw-actor header (signed). we'll share guidance in the security doc.
[07:38] Maya: perfect. another topic: model fallback - we need to fall back to lower-capacity models when load spikes. how are rollouts handled?
[07:46] Lina: Redwood supports rollout policies - canary, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained. This is configurable per-route. You can define latency SLOs and Redwood will route to a variant if the primary can't meet SLO.
[08:03] Roberto: good. do rollouts integrate with LangChain calls or at the gateway level?
[08:08] Arjun: rollout is server-side - no client changes needed. your LangChain chains hit the same endpoint and the platform handles routing.
[08:17] Maya: about SDK versions - we saw notes that older node SDKs had header name mismatch; what's current stable?
[08:25] Lina: v2.1.1 is the stable release with trace and rate header fixes. we'll attach changelog.
[08:33] Maya: great. can you share a short demo notebook showing LangChain sequence with embedding + retrieval using our sample prompt?
[08:40] Samir: yes Lina will send that. Lina, can you show the code quickly - just high-level?
[08:46] Lina: sure - example: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY')) - then LangChain wrapper: LLMRedwood(client, model='rw-llama-7b'); for LlamaIndex we create a RedwoodEmbeddings class, ingest docs, then query. I'll include the notebook link in the follow-up.
[09:05] Roberto: cool. any gotchas when running behind a proxy that rewrites bodies?
[09:11] Arjun: yes - keep request bodies intact for streaming and ensure chunked transfer is preserved. proxies that buffer entire responses will add latency and break streaming. we recommend pass-through streaming for real-time features.
[09:26] Maya: rate-limiting strategy - we want token-based throttling, not request-count only. support that?
[09:33] Lina: yes you can set token-based quotas. the headers expose remaining token budget. we also support burst windows and leaky-bucket style enforcement.
[09:46] Emily: compliance - do you do data retention controls? ability to opt-out of telemetry for specific orgs?
[09:52] Samir: yes customers can set retention windows and opt-out of telemetry; for Dedicated/Private you control log retention entirely. Hosted customers can request reduced retention and opt-out for PII. we'll attach the policy document.
[10:06] Maya: okay, timeline - we want a short POC before EOW to validate latency and integration. is that feasible?
[10:13] Arjun: feasible if you can provide sample prompts and allow a small pilot reservation. we'll need the prompt set and estimated QPS by Friday.
[10:22] Maya: we can do that. we'll also share the security questionnaire.
[10:27] Samir: perfect. any other questions?
[10:30] Roberto: one more - billing and internal cost attribution; can Redwood export per-team cost CSVs?
[10:36] Lina: yes exportable cost reports per API key/team; also usage APIs if you want to build internal dashboards.
[10:44] Kai: about observability hooks - can we push token-level metrics into our Datadog?
[10:49] Arjun: we have a Datadog integration that exports key metrics; otherwise you can pull via usage API and push custom metrics.
[11:00] Maya: awesome. that covers my main list.
[11:04] Samir: recap - Samir to send pricing & Dedicated options, Lina to send LangChain/LlamaIndex notebook and proxy samples, Arjun to schedule/prepare latency bench, Nova to send sample prompts and security questionnaire. we'll aim to reconvene after bench results.
[11:20] Emily: thanks everyone.
[11:22] Maya: thanks, talk soon.
[11:25] [call ends at 16:18 UTC]
